newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- off, pausing for breath?.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- off, pausing for breath?.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices edged down slightly in early trade on Thursday, taking a bit of a pause after recent strong gains, and cash prices resisted slipping as much as futures contracts.
"It's probably off maybe an 0.01," a trader estimated, referring to cash municipal bonds. "It's just a pause. We're going to take a breather. Everything's run up so much."
Another trader added "Cash is quiet, probably firmer than futures." He explained that both supplies and dealers' inventories were fairly light.
A closely followed yardstick of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, stood at just over $1 billion, a level considered fairly lean.

In early activity, a few customer bid-wanted lists were starting to circulate. The market was looking ahead to about $362 million in 17 sales scheduled for Thursday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $197 million in seven sales, with a $100 million Port Authority of New York & New Jersey deal through Lehman Brothers topping the list.
On the competitive side, 10 sales totaling $165 million were scheduled. A $40 million Kansas City deal at 1000 EDT was the largest.
Treasury prices initially firmed after the Labor Department found an unexpected surge in jobless claims, which jumped to 377,000 in the week ended July 5 from 337,000 a week earlier.
But the market retreated just as fast as economists said this was not a sign of a weakening economy, but instead reflected expected shutdowns at car-makers as they retool to make new models.
Fixed-income markets also were starting to anticipate the release on Friday of Producer Prices for June, which were forecast at unchanged, according to a Reuters consensus survey of economists.
In the secondary market for municipal bonds, bids on Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 100, unchanged.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority Massachusetts General Transportation of 2027, which have a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.42 percent, NET, down one basis point.
Municipal futures for September fell seven ticks to 119-4/32, while September Treasury bond futures shed nine ticks to 113-20/32.
The MOB spread widened to 176 ticks from 174 at the close on Wednesday.
